- Brown-to-tan lesion centered at a node/junction
- Leaves at the node are dead, brown, and desiccated
- No visible white mycelium (rules out Sclerotinia, Southern Blight)
- No obvious black coloring with concentric rings (less likely Alternaria)

The reference image for Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato shows internal stem browning/vascular discoloration with dead leaves all around — consistent with the test image's external brown canker at the node with completely desiccated/dead leaves.

The test image matches Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato because:
- Brown canker lesion centered at the stem node
- Dead, desiccated leaves at the infection site (classic defoliation symptom)
- Stem is otherwise green/intact (consistent with localized canker, not full collapse)
- No white mycelium visible (rules out Sclerotinia, Southern Blight)
- No gray sporulation (rules out Gray Mold)
- No obvious concentric rings near soil line (less likely Alternaria stem canker)
